merger_description:
Energy Bay Kappa Fund Pty Ltd as trustee for the Energy Bay Kappa Fund (**Energy Bay**) proposes to acquire from various subsidiaries of the Centuria Capital Group (the **CCG Members**):

* energy infrastructure assets and the exclusive right to operate existing embedded networks at 45 sites,
* energy infrastructure assets and the exclusive right to install and operate embedded networks at a further 194 sites, and
* first and last rights of refusal to acquire analogous rights in respect of any further sites of the kind described in the transaction documents provided as part of the application.

Energy Bay is part of Energy Bay Group, which is a distributed energy infrastructure company operating embedded networks at large commercial and industrial sites owned by third parties in New South Wales (**NSW**), Australian Capital Territory (**ACT**), Western Australia (**WA**), Victoria (**VIC**) and Queensland (**QLD**). Energy Bay Group also owns Diamond Energy Pty Ltd, an electricity retailer that operates in all National Electricity Market jurisdictions.

The CCG Members are subsidiaries of the Centuria Capital Group, which is comprised of Centuria Capital Limited and Centuria Funds Management Limited. The CCG Members invest in and manage properties for investment funds. As part of that primary business activity, in each of NSW, ACT, VIC, QLD, South Australia, and WA, they currently:

* operate embedded network infrastructure at some of their sites,
* engage in behind the meter generation or storage at their sites, and
* supply and sell electricity to their commercial tenants connected to their embedded networks.

Unlike Energy Bay the CCG Members do not, and do not plan to, operate embedded network infrastructure owned by third parties and/or at properties owned/occupied by third parties on behalf of those third parties.

determination_table_content.details:
Energy Bay Kappa Fund Pty Ltd as trustee for the Energy Bay Kappa
Fund (Energy Bay) proposes to acquire certain assets required to
operate embedded networks for 239 sites owned by members of the
Centuria Capital Group (CCG Members) (the Parties) (the
Acquisition)]

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Energy Bay is part of Energy Bay Group, which is a distributed energy
infrastructure company operating embedded networks at large
commercial and industrial sites owned by third parties across New
South Wales, Australian Capital Territory, Western Australia, Victoria
and Queensland.
The CCG Members are subsidiaries of the Centuria Capital Group,
which is comprised of Centuria Capital Limited and Centuria Funds
Management Limited. The CCG Members invest in and manage
properties for investment funds. As part of managing the properties,
CCG Members also operate the embedded networks.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The Parties both supply the following services in New South Wales,
Australian Capital Territory, Victoria, Queensland and Western
Australia:
• distribution of electricity within embedded networks
• retail supply of electricity to occupiers connected to those
networks
• generation and/or storage of electricity at embedded network
sites, with that electricity generated and/or stored then supplied
and sold to the owner or occupier and its commercial tenants,
together the EN Customer Services.
The CCG Members also supply EN Customer Services in South
Australia.
Energy Bay supplies EN Customer Services to third party customers
only. The CCG Members supply EN Customer Services to
commercial tenants of sites owned by the CCG Members only and
do not supply to any third parties.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties each supply EN Customer Services, however, Energy
Bay supplies to third party customers, whereas the CCG
Members only supply to commercial tenants of sites owned by
the CCG Members and do not supply to any third parties.
• As such, there are no relevant competitive overlaps between
Energy Bay and the CCG Members.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
